title: Quantification of 3‑chloro-7‑hydroxy-4-methylcoumarin (CHMC) in urine as a biomarker of coumaphos exposure by high-performance liquid chromatography-fluorescence detection (HPLC-FLD)
author: Robbins, Striley, et al.

steps.title: Prepare CHMC stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve CHMC to obtain an approximate concentration of 500.0 µg/mL in a 25 mL volumetric flask containing 10 mmol sodium acetate in deionized water; adjust to pH 5.3.

steps.title: Make intermediate calibration standard
steps.instruction: Add approximately 500 µL of the stock solution to a 10 mL volumetric flask and bring to volume with 10 mmol sodium acetate in deionized water to give an approximate concentration of 25.0 µg/mL.

steps.title: Create spiking calibration standards series
steps.instruction: Prepare a series of ten spiking calibration standards by serial dilution in 4 mL borosilicate glass vials.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the highest spiking standard by mixing 1 mL of the intermediate calibration standard with 1 mL of 10 mmol sodium acetate in deionized water.

Serially dilute the highest standard 1:1 (v/v) with 1 mL of 10 mmol sodium acetate in deionized water to generate standards with concentrations of 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.39, 0.78, 1.56, 3.13, 6.25, and 12.50 µg/mL.

steps.title: Prepare urine and aqueous calibration standards
steps.instruction: For urine standards, add 20 µL of each spiking calibration standard to 980 µL pooled control urine, yielding urine calibration concentrations of 0.49, 0.98, 1.95, 3.91, 7.81, 15.63, 31.26, 62.52, 125.04, and 250.07 ng/mL. For aqueous standards used in validation, add 20 µL of each spiking standard to 980 µL of 10 mmol sodium acetate in deionized water:acetonitrile (65:35 v/v).

steps.title: Store solutions at -20 °C
steps.instruction: Keep the stock solution and all calibration standards at –20 °C until use.

steps.title: Condition SPE cartridges
steps.instruction: Using Strata‑X‑A 33 µm polymeric strong anion‑exchange tubes (200 mg/3 mL) on a Fluka 16‑port vacuum manifold, pre‑condition each tube with 2 mL methanol followed by 2 mL 100 mmol ammonium acetate in deionized water.

steps.title: Load, wash, and elute samples on SPE
steps.instruction: Process the centrifuged urine supernatant through the conditioned SPE tubes.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant from each 15 mL polypropylene centrifuge tube to a pre‑conditioned SPE tube.
Wash the tube with 2 mL 100 mmol ammonium acetate in deionized water.
Wash the tube with 2 mL methanol.
Dry the cartridge under vacuum for 5 min.
Elute analyte with 3 mL 5 % formic acid in methanol into a 15 mL polypropylene centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Evaporate eluate under nitrogen
steps.instruction: Dry the eluate under nitrogen gas at 10 psi in a 50 °C water bath using a TurboVap® LV automated solvent evaporation system.

steps.title: Reconstitute extracts and transfer to vials
steps.instruction: Reconstitute each dried sample in 500 µL of 10 mmol sodium acetate in deionized water:acetonitrile (65:35 v/v), vortex, and transfer to 2 mL glass autosampler vials for HPLC‑FLD analysis.

description: The HPLC-FLD chromatograms of CHMC fluorescence for a control urine blank, a control urine calibration standard spiked with 7.81 ng/mL CHMC, and a worker post-shift urine sample with a calculated concentration of 7.5 ng/mL CHMC are shown in Fig. 2. The retention time of CHMC with the described HPLC gradient method was approximately 7.7 min. The baseline fluorescence noise at λex 355 nm excitation / λem 460 nm emission was approximately 0.2 luminescence units (LU) in both pooled control urine and in workers’ urine samples for the duration of the LC gradient program.Fig. 2Representative chromatograms of control urine blanks, CHMC standards spiked into control urine prior to sample preparation (7.81 ng/mL on left; 62.52 ng/mL on right), and two urine samples obtained from workers with calculated CHMC concentrations of 7.46 ng/mL (on left) and 75.24 ng/mL (on right).Fig. 2 The calculated average response factor for the calibration curve prepared in pooled control urine was 0.5 with a range of 0.46 – 0.56 and an RSD of 6.9 %. The calibration curve was linear from 0.49 – 250.07 ng/mL (N = 10) with a correlation coefficient of r = 0.9988 (CORREL function in Microsoft Excel). The calculated average response factor for the calibration curve prepared in 10 mmol sodium acetate in deionized water:acetonitrile (65:35 v/v) solution was 0.5 with a range of 0.48 – 0.56 (N = 10), an RSD of 6.3 %, and a correlation coefficient of r = 0.9997. The calculated MDLs and MDLb were 0.06 ng/mL and 0.03 ng/mL, respectively. Therefore, 0.06 ng/mL was chosen as the MDL. The Ss of 0.02 ng/mL for the MDLs replicate spiked samples was used to calculate the LOQ of 0.20 ng/mL. Because the calculated LOQ was lower than the calibration curve range, the lowest level calibration standard was treated as the lower limit of quantitation (LLOQ = 0.49 ng/mL) [23].
